title: Databases
description: Store, retrieve, and manage persistent data — the backbone of every application.
body:
## What is it?

A **database** is an organized collection of data that persists beyond a single program run. Two main families:

- **Relational (SQL)**: Data in tables with rows and columns. Examples: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite
- **Non-relational (NoSQL)**: Data in documents, key-value pairs, or graphs. Examples: MongoDB, Redis, Firestore

## When to use which

| SQL (PostgreSQL) | NoSQL (MongoDB) |
|-----------------|-------------------|
| Complex relationships | Flexible schemas |
| Financial data (ACID) | High write volume |
| Reporting & analytics | Mobile & IoT data |
| Most web apps | Real-time data |

## Key SQL concepts

```sql
-- Create table
CREATE TABLE users (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, email TEXT UNIQUE);

-- Insert
INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES ('Alice', 'alice@example.com');

-- Query
SELECT * FROM users WHERE name LIKE 'A%' ORDER BY name;

-- Join
SELECT posts.title, users.name
FROM posts JOIN users ON posts.user_id = users.id;
```
